name: Amogus Club
description: Rutgers' home for Among Us and social deduction games. Gather your crewmates, finish your tasks, and figure out who's acting sus before the impostor gets you.
mission: Amogus Club brings students together over Among Us and other social deduction games. We host lobby nights where crewmates and impostors face off, custom-rules rounds like Hide and Seek and proximity chat, and the occasional real-life Among Us game across campus with tasks, emergency meetings, and plenty of accusations. You don't need to be good at lying or at spotting liars to join: new players learn the maps, tasks, and voting etiquette in friendly beginner lobbies. Whether you mostly vent, mostly report bodies, or just like yelling "that's sus" at your friends, there's a spot on the ship for you.
location: To be announced by the club officers
meeting_schedule: To be announced by the club officers
eligibility: Open to all Rutgers students. No Among Us experience needed.

faqs.question: Do I need to own Among Us?
faqs.answer: Among Us is free on mobile, so you can join lobby nights from your phone. Real-life games need no device at all.

faqs.question: I've never played. Can I still join?
faqs.answer: Yes. Beginner lobbies walk new crewmates through the maps, tasks, and how emergency meetings and voting work.

faqs.question: What is a real-life Among Us game?
faqs.answer: Players get secret roles and complete small tasks around a building while impostors try to tag them. Anyone can call an emergency meeting to discuss and vote someone out.
